chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Nakhaʿī, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A cow suffices for five at Minā when they are people of one table.

key_terms.أَهْلَ خِوَانٍ وَاحِدٍ: people of one table, meaning those joined in a shared household or common provision
key_terms.الْبَقَرَةُ: a cow used here as the sacrificial animal
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the hajj ritual site where sacrifice is performed
key_terms.تُجْزِي: is sufficient or valid in fulfillment of the required offering
key_terms.خَمْسَةٍ: five persons sharing in the offering

ai.seo_question: When does one cow suffice for five people at Minā?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning sacrificial sharing at Minā during hajj. It states that one cow is sufficient on behalf of five people, provided they are united in one household or shared table.
